title_yt: What If You Earned $3,858 Every Second? #Shorts
title_fb: What if you earned thousands of dollars every second? GTA 5 did, by estimates
hook: What if you earned three thousand dollars every second?
open_loop: The hook promises thousands of dollars per second; the viewer wonders who earns that. Answer (GTA 5 estimated sales, about $3,858 a second) comes in lines 4-5, and the final lemonade-cup comparison and the GTA 6 question pay off in the last ~8 s.
payoff: About $1B in 3 days is about $333M a day, about $3,858 a second, almost 4,000 lemonade cups every second.

lines.text: What if you earned *three thousand dollars every second?
lines.say: What if you earned three thousand dollars every second?
lines.visual: Frame 0: Benny (money outfit) stands smug, flipping a coin; gold counter already ticking up to $3,000 beside a small wall clock. Snap-zoom on 'three thousand'; counter bumps on 'second'.

lines.text: You sell lemonade for *one dollar a cup.
lines.say: You sell lemonade for one dollar a cup.
lines.visual: Benny behind a tiny wooden lemonade stand, happy, holds a cup; clink sfx; badge '$1 A CUP'. Hop on 'one dollar'.

lines.text: Then a giant *register opens next door.
lines.say: Then a giant register opens next door.
lines.visual: Whoosh. A huge generic cartoon cash register (cash prop, big scale, no logos) slams in on the right with thud sfx and camera shake; Benny shocked, lemonade cup flies off. Bubble 'WHAT?!'.

lines.text: GTA 5 made *about *one *billion dollars in three days.
lines.say: G, T, A five made about one billion dollars in three days.
lines.visual: Benny in worry pose beside a plain white outlined text 'GTA 5' (plain text only, no logo); gold counter climbs to $1 BILLION; badge 'ESTIMATED SALES'; stamp '3 DAYS'; cash rains from the register.

lines.text: Every second is about *three thousand, eight hundred fifty-eight dollars.
lines.say: Every second is about three thousand, eight hundred fifty-eight dollars.
lines.visual: Benny stares at a wall clock; each tick (tick sfx) the register spits a cash stack with ding and a '+$3,858' badge; Benny scoops with both hands, cash flying past. Gold counter to $3,858 with 'ABOUT'.

lines.text: You try to count, but cannot *keep up.
lines.say: You try to count, but cannot keep up.
lines.visual: Benny runs in place with a notepad, brain-panic, dizzy; expression shocked then broke; cash piles over his head; fast ticks; thought bubble '1... 2...?!'.

lines.text: One second of sales equals *almost *four thousand cups.
lines.say: One second of sales equals almost four thousand cups.
lines.visual: Benny slumps small at his stand. Bar 'YOUR STAND: 1 CUP' stays tiny beside a huge bar '1 SECOND: ABOUT 3,858 CUPS'; coins rain; Benny shrugs, broke expression.

lines.text: Will *GTA *6 beat it? Comment *yes or no.
lines.say: Will G, T, A six beat it? Comment yes or no.
lines.visual: Benny points at the viewer, smug; plain white outlined text 'GTA 6?' (no art); list rows 'YES' and 'NO'; gold headline 'COMMENT YES OR NO'. Hard cut after the last word (tail ~0.3 s).

facts_used.claim: GTA 5 made over $1 billion in its first 3 days (retail sales estimate, record at the time).
GTA 6 releases November 19, 2026 (hype context for the ending question).

math_check: Python: $1,000,000,000 / 3 days = $333,333,333 per day; / 86,400 s = $3,858.02 per second (about $3,858). One $1 cup per $1 => about 3,858 cups per second ('almost four thousand'). Speech skips the per-day step to stay under 75 words; the hook's 'three thousand' is a rounded-down hypothetical, exact figure said in line 5.
word_count_note: Counted on the 'say' field (G, T, A five = 4 words).
ip_notes: 'GTA' appears only as plain spoken/written topic text. No Rockstar characters, logos, lettering, footage, art or music. The register is a generic cartoon cash register.

upload.description:
A lemonade stand vs the money GTA 5 made every single second. 🍋
Will GTA 6 beat it? Comment YES or NO!
By sales estimates, GTA 5 made about $1 billion in its first 3 days. That is about $333 million a day, or about $3,858 every second.
Source: Engadget, Shacknews. Estimated retail sales, not exact.
